title: Beyond the 956: Gloria Steinem, feminist icon and Ms. magazine co-founder, dies at 92

content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Gloria Steinem, the celebrated author and activist who became one of the most visible voices of the U.S. women’s movement and a co-founder of Ms. magazine, has died at 92.

Steinem, who had been in declining health, died Wednesday, November 25, 2026, at her home in New York City, according to a post on her social media page. No cause of death was disclosed.

Born Gloria Marie Steinem on March 25, 1934, in Toledo, Ohio, she began her career as a journalist. In 1963, she went undercover as a Playboy Bunny for an exposé of degrading conditions in Hugh Hefner’s Playboy empire. Six years later, covering an abortion rights hearing in 1969 changed the course of her life — she had undergone a secret illegal abortion herself at 22 — and she became a women’s rights activist.

In 1971, Steinem founded the National Women’s Political Caucus along with Betty Friedan, Shirley Chisholm and Bella Abzug. The following year, she co-founded Ms. magazine, which many commentators dismissed as a passing fad; she stayed with the magazine as an adviser after it was bought in 2001 by the Feminist Majority Foundation.

For more than six decades, Steinem traveled the country speaking at college campuses, community centers, rallies and marches, championing equality for women and a wide range of causes. Her books included the 2015 road memoir A Life on the Road — though she wryly noted she had never learned to drive. In 2017, she was the keynote speaker at the historic Women’s March in Washington. Her life was the subject of the 2020 feature film The Glorias, A Life on the Road, and at 91 she collaborated on the picture book Rise, Girl, Rise with Liberian peace activist and Nobel laureate Leymah Gbowee.

“Being a feminist means that you see the world as whole instead of half,” she once said. “It shouldn’t need a name, and one day it won’t.”

Steinem never had children, and said she never regretted it. In 2000, she married at 66, to British activist and businessman David Bale, the father of actor Christian Bale; he died in 2003.

Sources: The Associated Press; The Well News; statement from Gloria Steinem’s social media page.
